name: Monoamine Oxidase A Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of impulsive aggressive behavior and mild intellectual disability
Reduced monoamine oxidase A enzymatic activity in platelets or fibroblasts
Pathogenic variants in the MAOA gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
X-linked inheritance pattern with affected males and carrier females

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical features plus reduced MAOA enzymatic activity and confirmation of pathogenic MAOA gene variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic and enzymatic testing due to overlap with other neuropsychiatric disorders.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic behavioral phenotype including sudden outbursts of aggression
Cognitive impairment typically in the mild range
Increased levels of serotonin and dopamine metabolites in urine

common.notes: Generalized or focal seizures reported in some patients
Including insomnia and altered sleep architecture
Rapid mood swings and emotional lability
Delayed language development in early childhood

occasional.notes: Social interaction difficulties and repetitive behaviors
Reduced muscle tone observed in infancy
Symptoms such as constipation or delayed gastric emptying

rare.notes: Involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal postures
Rare reports of irregular heart rhythms
Sensorineural hearing loss in isolated cases

laboratory: Reduced monoamine oxidase A enzymatic activity in platelets or fibroblasts
Elevated urinary levels of serotonin and dopamine metabolites
imaging: Brain MRI typically normal or nonspecific findings
other: X-linked inheritance pattern with affected males and carrier females

distinguishingFeatures: Also caused by MAOA deficiency but sometimes considered synonymous
Affects MAOB enzyme, different clinical presentation
Lacks enzymatic and genetic abnormalities in MAOA
Broader range of social communication deficits

redFlags: Severe impulsive aggression leading to harm
Early onset mild intellectual disability with behavioral abnormalities
Family history of X-linked neuropsychiatric disorder
references: Brunner HG, Nelen M, Breakefield XO, Ropers HH, van Oost BA. Abnormal behavior associated with a point mutation in the structural gene for monoamine oxidase A. Science. 1993 Dec 3;262(5133):578-80.
Shih JC, Chen K, Ridd MJ. Monoamine oxidase: from genes to behavior. Annu Rev Neurosci. 1999;22:197-217.

Cases O, Seif I, Grimsby J, Gaspar P, Chen K, Pournin S, et al. Aggressive behavior and altered amounts of brain serotonin and norepinephrine in mice lacking MAOA. Science. 1995 Jan 27;268(5218):1763-6.
